quality.hardDesign: 결론이 직접 제시되지 않고 (1)전통적 판단 기준 (2)이미징 결과로 드러난 예외적 패턴 (3)Voss 본인의 창작 습관에 대한 증언 (4)확정된 진작과의 대조까지 네 요소를 모두 연결해야 정답을 도출할 수 있다. unlike를 이용한 대조 단서를 추가해 '표기가 있고 수정 흔적도 있는 경우'와 '표기만 있고 수정 흔적이 없는 경우'를 혼동하면 오답을 고르게 되며, 각 오답은 지운 흔적/이미징 조사/귀속 문제라는 지문 요소를 하나씩 공유하지만 논리적 방향이 다르게 설계되었다.

problem.passage:
Musicologists studying the manuscript traditions of the eighteenth-century composer Elena Voss have long relied on a notational habit known as the compressed cadenza marking, a shorthand of slurred sixteenth notes that Voss used to indicate ornamental flourishes without writing out every pitch. For years, the presence of this shorthand in a manuscript was treated as strong evidence that the score had been copied out by Voss's own hand rather than by a hired copyist, since copyists were assumed to lack the intimate familiarity with her improvisational style needed to abbreviate passages so confidently without risking errors. Multispectral imaging of several disputed manuscripts has recently revealed, however, that a number of scores bearing this shorthand also contain extensive erased and rewritten measures beneath the ink, a pattern of correction that Voss herself, according to her students' letters, almost never produced because she dictated finished passages fluently and rarely revised once notes were set down. Unlike scores confirmed to be in Voss's hand, which show almost no erasure beneath the shorthand passages, these disputed manuscripts suggest a different process of composition altogether, one in which the shorthand was added only after a slower, corrected process of working out the music underneath. If future analysis of an unattributed manuscript reveals the compressed cadenza shorthand but shows no erased or rewritten measures beneath it at all, ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Musicologists studying the manuscript traditions of the eighteenth-century composer Elena Voss have long relied on a notational habit known as the compressed cadenza marking, a shorthand of slurred sixteenth notes that Voss used to indicate ornamental flourishes without writing out every pitch. For years, the presence of this shorthand in a manuscript was treated as strong evidence that the score had been copied out by Voss's own hand rather than by a hired copyist, since copyists were assumed to lack the intimate familiarity with her improvisational style needed to abbreviate passages so confidently without risking errors. Multispectral imaging of several disputed manuscripts has recently revealed, however, that a number of scores bearing this shorthand also contain extensive erased and rewritten measures beneath the ink, a pattern of correction that Voss herself, according to her students' letters, almost never produced because she dictated finished passages fluently and rarely revised once notes were set down. Unlike scores confirmed to be in Voss's hand, which show almost no erasure beneath the shorthand passages, these disputed manuscripts suggest a different process of composition altogether, one in which the shorthand was added only after a slower, corrected process of working out the music underneath. If future analysis of an unattributed manuscript reveals the compressed cadenza shorthand but shows no erased or rewritten measures beneath it at all, ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the absence of erased and rewritten measures would strengthen the case for attributing the manuscript to Voss herself rather than to a copyist
the manuscript would likely be judged musically inferior to works securely attributed to Voss
musicologists would need to reexamine every previously confirmed Voss manuscript for similar erasures
the compressed cadenza shorthand would be shown to have originated with one of Voss's copyists rather than with Voss
problem.explanation: 지문은 여러 문장을 종합해야 한다: (1) 압축 카덴차 표기가 있으면 전통적으로 Voss 본인의 필사로 간주되었지만, (2) 다중분광 이미징 결과 이 표기가 있는 일부 악보에서 지워지고 다시 쓴 마디들이 발견되었으며, (3) Voss 본인은 즉흥적으로 완성된 악절을 유창하게 받아 적어 거의 수정하지 않았다는 증언이 있고, (4) Voss 본인 필사로 확정된 악보들은 이 표기 아래에 지운 흔적이 거의 없다는 대조가 제시된다. 따라서 표기는 있지만 지우고 고친 흔적이 전혀 없는 악보는 오히려 Voss 본인의 특징적 작업 방식(수정 없이 바로 완성)과 일치하므로 Voss 본인 귀속을 강화하는 증거가 된다 - A. B는 '지운 흔적'이라는 소재는 공유하지만 귀속 문제를 예술적 우열이라는 무관한 방향으로 바꾼 오개념(부분 일치)이다. C는 다중분광 이미징이라는 방법은 맞지만, 지문은 이미 확정된 필사본들이 애초에 지운 흔적이 없다고 명시하므로 재검토가 필요하다는 근거가 없는 과도한 확장이다. D는 지문이 전혀 뒷받침하지 않는 원인·결과 전도로, 표기법의 기원을 필사자에게로 뒤바꾼다.
